reviewer: Claude review agent, independent of the extraction agent; no human review claimed

extraction_reviewed.note: The task named commit 2ec78cd. That commit was amended to 8a2a61c while this review was reading the batch; the amendment dropped an obsolete note about issue #177 from build_coverage.py, coverage.json and research.md. Every hash in this receipt is of the bytes reviewed and added.

method: Independent re-check of an extracted batch against its pinned sources, following docs/collection.md section 5 and .agents/skills/review-evidence/SKILL.md. All seven source artifacts were re-retrieved and their SHA-256 recomputed. Text layers and parsers were written for this review; the extraction pass's own modules were not rerun, so the value check is independent of the code that produced the values.

scope.automated_comparison: Every result's and claim's printed_value was checked for verbatim presence in its own source's bytes (198 of 198 found), and every quoted sentence in a source_locator was checked verbatim against the source with a parser written for this review. 71 locators carry a prose quotation of more than 40 characters; one failed and was corrected. The remaining misses were multi-line PDF table column headers that no contiguous-string test can match, and each was confirmed by reading the table.
scope.manual_sample: All 81 AlphaProteo results were read cell by cell against Table 1, Table S2 and Table S3 in an independently generated text layer, and all 36 Bennett results against Supplementary Methods Table 6. That is 117 of 159 results checked by eye against the table, not a sample. The 24 BindCraft and 18 Adaptyv results sit in prose and were checked by the verbatim quotation test plus a reading of each cited passage.
scope.recomputation: No result in the batch carries a derivation, so there was nothing to rerun. BindCraft Supplementary Data 1 was reparsed independently to test the extraction pass's refusal to compute per-target rates from it; the refusal holds (see findings).
not_checked: Figures were not read, by this review or by the extraction pass: BindCraft Fig. 1b, Adaptyv Figures 3, 8, 9 and 10, AlphaProteo Figures 1D, 1E and S1 to S7, Bennett Extended Data Fig. 10. They remain recorded gaps.

The sources behind AlphaProteo's compilation rows (Procko, Gainza, Cao, Berger, Yang, Watson) were not retrieved by either pass, so the published RFdiffusion rates this review rules on could not be checked against their own primary source.
No value was reproduced experimentally and no model was run.

limitations: This is automated AI review. It is not human scientific review, it is not reproduction, and it is not experimental replication. What it establishes is that each stored value matches the pinned source at the stated locator, that the nulls are genuinely unstated, and that the relevance judgements, exclusions and summary describe what the sources actually support. It cannot establish that the sources' own measurements are correct. Independent human scientific review of this use case remains outstanding.

uc-binder-20261022-source-adaptyv-prepri.note: FINDING, not reconciled by changing the hash. validation.records_add: 420 records added; conform to the SHACL shapes.
validation.test_fast: 43 files, 386 tests, all passed. tests/omics-coverage-floor.test.ts passed here in 8.2s; the extraction pass saw it fail in its own worktree on a missing release asset under data/omics/releases/, which is populated in this worktree. No test was skipped.

changes_after_add.note: Made after the batch was in the store, so each went through npm run records -- change with this review, and the affected claims were repinned. The BindCraft 46.3% finding was raised by the team lead and verified independently here.

records.reason: The printed 46.3% cannot be reproduced from the paper's own per-target counts: the ten printed rates sum to 526.613439 pp, a displayed 46.3% over twelve targets needs [555.0, 556.2), so CrSAS-6 (of 9) and CbAgo (of 12) would have to contribute [28.3866, 29.5866), and no integer pair does. A pooled rate over 156 designs does not fit either. The source states only "an average success rate of 46.3%" and never defines the basis. The stored value is unchanged. Recorded at result level rather than as a sixth source-level evidence_concerns entry, for the reason given in the dated review.

The protocol's aggregation and comparison_limit fields assert an unweighted mean over twelve targets; the source states only "average". The limitation records that those fields are the extraction pass's reading, not a stated basis. aggregation and metric_qualifier were left unchanged as pinned comparison fields.

Adds that a headline average is not always recoverable from the per-target numbers the same paper prints, so averages are not comparable across papers. exclusions is pinned, so all 16 claims were repinned.
